query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Partial replacement of Ni by up to 10 at.% Co in MnNiSi alloys, fabricated via arc melting and homogenization, will enhance mechanical performance without significantly diminishing their magnetocaloric effect in the 280–350 K temperature range.
generation.intervention: Partial Co substitution for Ni (0–10 at.%) in MnNiSi.
generation.conditions: Alloys produced by arc melting and homogenization annealing; magnetocaloric properties measured under a 1–2 T field and mechanical tests performed at room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Improved grain boundary cohesion and modified lattice parameters driven by Co substitution.
generation.mechanism: The Co dopant atoms suppress brittle fracture through enhanced lattice stability and improved ductility, preventing substantial deterioration of the magnetocaloric effect by preserving the magnetically active Mn–X–Si framework.
generation.predicted_outcome: Higher yield strength and fracture toughness relative to the undoped MnNiSi baseline, with <10% reduction in the maximum magnetic entropy change at the target operating temperatures (280–350 K).
generation.baseline: MnNiSi alloy without Co substitution, prepared under the same conditions.
generation.boundary: Substitution beyond 10 at.% Co or variations in annealing protocol may alter the magnetostructural transition and degrade the magnetocaloric effect.
generation.uncertainty: Direct experimental evidence for Co doping of MnNiSi is limited, so the potential trade-off between mechanical properties and magnetocaloric performance remains to be empirically confirmed.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare MnNiSi and MnNi(1−x)CoxSi alloys at x = 0, 0.02, 0.05, and 0.10 via arc melting; anneal for homogeneity; measure Vickers hardness and tensile/compressive properties alongside magnetization under 1–2 T from 280–350 K to evaluate magnetocaloric effect.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is refuted if Co-doped MnNiSi samples do not show higher mechanical strength and/or exhibit a reduction in magnetocaloric effect exceeding 10% relative to the undoped baseline under the same conditions.
